text: I've been watching this company all morning. Projects, people, machines, finance. Everyone is so busy!
Busy, yes. Connected? Not really. Every team has its own sheet, and its own version of the truth.
So that's why they keep calling each other!
Now picture them all on one platform. Meet Synax ERP.
Projects, people, and the shop floor? In one place?
Projects, staffing, HR, manufacturing, quality and finance. Each team gets its own workspace, on shared data.
Okay, you have my attention. Show me!
How does a manager know if a project is actually making money?
The team logs its hours in the Work Tracker, and Cost Mapper brings the project's costs together.
And billing?
Billing and dev cost review sit right beside it. Project analytics shows the whole picture.
New scenario. A client needs three Java developers by Monday!
That's a requirement under a statement of work. Then candidates, interviews and offers, onboarding and deployment.
So hiring is just the beginning?
Exactly. Work logs and timesheets lead to invoices and payments, with replacements and an audit trail on record.
And the people inside the company? Attendance, leave, the usual chaos?
Follow Maya. A manpower request opens a job position. She's interviewed, gets an offer, and pre-joining checks are done before day one.
Does she get her own login?
Her own employee portal: attendance, leave, the holiday calendar and her documents. Then performance reviews, and one day, clearance, final settlement and an exit interview.
From hello to goodbye. Got it!
Now the serious part. A customer order comes in. Does everyone start phoning each other?
Not here. Let's follow one order. The customer P O is recorded, and contract review checks that we can deliver.
Do we even have the material?
Sales planning and the M R P run work it out. Anything short becomes a purchase requisition, then a vendor P O.
And when the truck arrives?
Gate control logs it, the G R N register books it in, and the material ledger holds the stock. Customer-owned material is tracked separately, for job work.
Now we make the parts?
A route card is generated against the bill of materials, material is issued, and jobs are scheduled. The load chart shows how busy each machine is.
What if a machine stops halfway?
Live monitoring shows every connected machine, and downtime and alarms record why it stopped.
I thought manufacturing was just machines making things!
And I thought birds didn't do paperwork.
Fair point. What if a part fails inspection?
Quality has its own workspace: final inspection and C O C, FAIR, N C R and CAPA, and calibration. Genealogy traces any part back through its history.
And then it ships?
Packing and dispatch, delivery challans with e-way bills, and the route cards move on to the invoice.
From order to truck. I need a moment.
Does it stop once the work is done?
No. Customer invoices with your own templates, debit and credit notes, project billing and staffing invoices.
Quick one. Who has the company laptop?
Check assets. Every asset is listed and assigned to a person.
And who decides who sees what?
Admins do, with roles, users, and page and feature permissions.
Last question. With all this data, who spots the problems?
Synax AI answers questions about your data, and Synax agents watch for exceptions, like overdue challans, and propose a fix.
Wait. They change things on their own?
No. Nothing changes until someone with the right role approves. And teams talk it through in chat and meetings.
Projects, people, manufacturing, finance. All connected?
That's the idea. Less juggling. More visibility. Better control.
Sounds like a smarter way to run a business!
Synax ERP. One platform. Connected business.
